checks.name: T1 point 10 ahead projects to screen centre
T2 same relative point gives the same pixel
T3 world -X is the player's RIGHT -> screen x > centre
T3 world +X is the player's LEFT -> screen x < centre
T4 +Y is ABOVE centre (screen y < centre)
T4 -Y is BELOW centre
T5 point behind is rejected (z > 0)
T6a with a per-display fov the normalised y is resolution-invariant
T6b a stale aspect in fov shifts the point (this is detectable at runtime)
T7 with w == 0 the same relative geometry gives the same pixel
T7 with w == camera the same relative geometry lands on DIFFERENT pixels
T7 the leak is proportional to the world position, not to the offset
T8 treating degrees as a multiplier collapses the aspect correction
T9 point 10 blocks down -X is at the centre
T9 -Z is the player's RIGHT when facing -X (screen x > centre)
T10 a point at the camera is rejected, not divided by zero
T11a equal parameter sets give an exactly identical pixel
T11b a 0.25-block origin difference moves the pixel by > 1 px
T11c a 5% fov drift moves the pixel by > 1 px
T11d equal parameters produce zero delta, and the selected perturbations are detectable
T12a w == -dot(axis, origin) classifies as DOUBLE_ORIGIN_SUBTRACTION_CONFIRMED
T12b the projection really shifts, so the duplication is not cosmetic
T12c an unexplained w is AFFINE_TRANSLATION_TERM_PRESENT and nothing more
T12d w == 0 is NO_TRANSLATION_TERM, not a silent pass
T13a an on-axis point keeps its pixel even with a 30% fov difference
T13b yet the two parameter sets are NOT equal -- fovsMatch would be false
T13c off-axis the same fov difference does move the pixel -- sensitivity, quantified
T14a production origin -> residual zero -> DOUBLE_ORIGIN_SUBTRACTION_CONFIRMED
T14b the stale transform origin misclassifies the same matrix
T14c the two verdicts disagree here, so the choice of origin is load-bearing
T15a the local player's render position is at the camera plane -> rejected
T15b a point behind the camera is rejected
T15c a non-finite coordinate is rejected
T15d an AABB corner below and beside the camera is accepted
T15e the picker skips every unusable candidate and returns the corner
T16a pairing stale matrix facts with a later control frame is refused
T16b facts read on the control frame pair, and both stamps are equal
T16c the paired block is self-contained: it carries the control frame's matrix
T17a eight distinct vertices, covering min and max on every axis
T17b a box whose only usable corners lie outside the old four is still found
T17c the old four were a strict subset: four vertices were never examined
T18a the off-axis point wins even though the on-axis one is listed first
T18b and its sensitivity score is strictly larger
T19a the local fallback is flagged from its source even though its raw score is high
T19b a nearly on-axis non-local point is flagged from its score
T19c an off-axis non-local point is OK, so screenDelta is usable there
T20a first search on the first frame, then no more often than the interval
T20b the budget counts searches, not frames
T20c after the budget the cadence drops to the slow retry interval

conventions.viewSpace: camera looks down -Z; z_v < 0 in front
conventions.rows: rows[0]=right, rows[1]=up, rows[2]=-forward, w must be 0
conventions.screen: sx = W/2 + W/2 * x_v/(depth*fovx); sy = H/2 - H/2 * y_v/(depth*fovy)
